chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, Zurarah, Ma'mar ibn Yahya, and Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

There is no recitation in the salat (prayer) over the deceased, nor any fixed supplication. You may supplicate with whatever occurs to you, and the most deserving of the dead to be supplicated for is the believer, and one should begin with salat upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: the funeral prayer performed over the deceased
key_terms.دُعَاءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ: a fixed or specifically prescribed supplication
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Is there a fixed recitation or specific du'a in the funeral prayer for the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that in the salat (prayer) over the deceased, there is no prescribed recitation and no fixed du'a (supplication) that must be said. Rather, one may supplicate freely, with special emphasis on supplicating for the deceased believer and beginning with salat upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
